transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant, and I keep starting the sanitation steps, or like, the batch logs and end-of-line paperwork... which, by the way, is a ton of paperwork. You really wouldn't think so, right? Like, I got my bachelor's degree thinking I'd be doing something completely different, maybe working in a lab or something, but the job market is just so weird right now. 

My roommate actually just got laid off from her tech job, which is crazy because she's so smart. We were just talking about it last night while making dinner. We made tacos, actually, using some of the ground beef I brought home from work with my employee discount. It's a pretty good perk, honestly. 

But wait, sorry, what was I... oh, right, work. Yeah, so I start the logs or the sanitation stuff, and I somehow just leave out the last parts. Like, every single time. Even when I know my job completely depends on finishing them correctly. I just don't finish them. And the floor manager gets so mad about the logs. He has this really loud cough, like a barking cough, and he always does it right when he's looking at my half-finished clipboard... but yeah, that's why I'm here. I keep leaving out the last parts of my tasks.

When you're doing those logs or sanitation steps and you stop before finishing them, do you feel like you *have to* stop or leave them incomplete, like there's an urge or pressure driving you to do it that way? Or does it feel more like you just lose focus or motivation and can't push yourself to finish?

No, it's definitely not like... an urge. I don't feel like I *have* to stop. It's more like... I just sort of drift away from it? Like, my brain just empties out, or I suddenly realize I'm staring at the wall, or thinking about something totally different. Like the other day, I was supposed to be finishing the batch log for the morning shift, and the next thing I know, I'm standing by the breakroom vending machine trying to decide if I want a Diet Coke or a Sprite. 

Which, by the way, our vending machine is always broken. It ate two of my dollars last week, and when I told the maintenance guy, Dave, he just shrugged. Dave is always wearing these neon orange shoelaces, even though we have a strict uniform policy. I don't know how he gets away with it. The floor manager is such a stickler for the rules, especially with the hairnets. I have really thick hair, so getting it all under the net is a whole process every morning. I usually have to use, like, ten bobby pins. 

But yeah, I don't feel pressured to leave the paperwork unfinished. I just... I don't know, the motivation just evaporates, and then I'm doing something else before I even realize I stopped working on the log.
Does this happen only at work, or do you find yourself leaving things unfinished in other parts of your life too — like at home, with personal projects, or in your relationships?

Um, I'm not really sure, actually. I haven't really thought about if it happens at home or with other stuff. I guess maybe? But my roommate usually handles a lot of the apartment stuff anyway, especially since she got laid off. She's been reorganizing our entire kitchen to pass the time. 

She bought all these clear plastic bins from Target... have you seen those? The ones where people on TikTok restock their fridges and it looks all perfectly aesthetic? We tried doing that with the fruit, but honestly, the strawberries just went bad so much faster. I read somewhere that you're not supposed to wash them until right before you eat them, but she washed all of them and put them in this little container with a paper towel. It was a total disaster. We had to throw out like a whole carton, which is so annoying because groceries are so expensive right now. Especially eggs! Though I guess eggs are coming down a little bit? I don't even know. I usually just eat cereal anyway. 

But um... yeah, I haven't really noticed if I leave things unfinished outside of work. I just don't really know.

When you were in school — elementary, middle, or high school — did you have similar problems with finishing assignments or leaving work incomplete, or was this something that only started more recently?

Oh, um... yeah, no, it's definitely not a new thing. Like, my mom actually still has my old elementary school report cards, especially from around fourth grade. She keeps literally everything. Her garage is just stacked with plastic bins of my old stuff, and my brother's stuff. He was obsessed with those little Tech Deck finger skateboards? Do you remember those? He had this huge plastic ramp set up in the living room and I was always stepping on them. They hurt so bad to step on, honestly almost worse than Legos. We used to fight about it all the time, and then my mom would threaten to vacuum them all up, but she never did because, like I said, she never throws anything away. 

But wait, sorry, the report cards. Right. So, on those fourth-grade report cards, the teachers wrote that I was really bright, but that I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn in my homework. I remember I would understand the lessons perfectly fine, but I'd just miss huge chunks of the instructions unless the teacher stayed really close to me. 

My teacher that year, Mrs. Higgins, she used to hover by my desk a lot. She wore this super strong floral perfume. It smelled exactly like the potpourri my grandma used to keep in a decorative bowl on her toilet tank. Why did people do that in the nineties? Just bowls of dried flowers in the bathroom. It just gets so dusty, and you can't even wash it. But yeah, if Mrs. Higgins wasn't standing right next to me smelling like dusty flowers, I would just completely miss what we were supposed to be finishing.

When you're doing things that require you to pay close attention — like reading a book, watching a movie, or having a conversation with someone — do you find yourself drifting away or losing focus in those situations too, or does this mainly happen with the paperwork and logs at work?

Um... yeah, it definitely happens with the work stuff, like a lot. Even when I start my shift trying really, really hard to stay locked in and focused. Like, I'll tell myself, "Okay, today we are paying attention." But after a while, all the cutting and weighing and checking the labels, it just all starts to blur together. And then I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the same tray of chicken breasts or the same log sheet for who knows how long, without actually taking in what I'm supposed to be doing next. 

Speaking of the chicken, they changed our supplier last month, and the new packaging is so annoying to open. It's supposed to be this easy-peel corner thing, but it never peels. You always have to use a knife anyway, which defeats the whole purpose. My coworker, Sarah, actually cut right through her glove trying to open one the other day. She didn't get hurt, thank god, because we wear those chainmail gloves underneath, but it ruined the top glove. We have to wear the blue nitrile ones over the chainmail, and my hands get so sweaty in them. By the end of the shift, it's like a swamp in there. I tried using this special lotion that's supposed to stop your hands from sweating—my roommate recommended it because she used it for her feet when she went to this outdoor music festival last summer. 

She went to Coachella, actually. Well, not Coachella, it was something like it, but in the Midwest. She said it was so dusty she had to wear a bandana over her face the whole time. She looked like a cowboy in all her Instagram pictures. But yeah, the lotion didn't work for my hands at all. It just made the gloves slide around more. 

But um, what were you asking? Oh, right, losing focus. Yeah, it just all blurs together at work and I end up staring at the trays not knowing what to do next.

When you're having a conversation with someone you care about, or watching a show you're really interested in, do you find yourself spacing out or losing track of what's being said, the way you do with the work logs?

Um... yeah, I guess it happens with conversations too. Like, not just with shows or whatever, but when people are talking right to me. Like with my supervisor at work. She'll be standing right in front of me giving me directions for the shift, and I'm looking right at her, nodding, making eye contact, like, "Yep, got it." But then a minute later she walks away and I realize I only remember the very first thing she said, and I have to go find Sarah and ask her what we were just told to do. 

Which is embarrassing because my supervisor is actually really intimidating. She has this crazy intense stare, and she wears these really bright red glasses. They're like, cat-eye shaped? I always wonder where she got them because they look vintage, but they could also just be from Zenni or one of those online glasses places. My roommate buys all her glasses online now. She has like six different pairs just to match her outfits. She even has this one pair that's completely clear, which I think makes her look like a scientist, but she says it's "chic." I tried them on once and I got an instant headache because the prescription was so strong. I don't even wear glasses, I just have perfectly fine vision, thank god, because contacts seem like a nightmare. You have to poke yourself in the eye every morning? No thank you. My brother used to sleep in his contacts and he got this horrible eye infection... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my supervisor. Yeah, she'll tell me what to do, I'll nod, and then I have no idea what she actually said.

When you're sitting down trying to work on those logs or do other tasks that require you to stay still, do you feel restless or fidgety? Do you find yourself having trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you need to get up and move around?

Um... no, not really. Like, I don't feel like I have to get up and run around or anything. I can sit still just fine. It's more just my brain that won't stay still, you know? Like, physically I'm okay sitting there with the logs. 

Actually, the chairs in the break room where we do the logs are surprisingly comfortable. They're those rolling office chairs, but they have this really nice lumbar support. I think they got them from a startup that went out of business down the street. It was this tech company that was supposed to be making some kind of app for dog walkers? Or maybe it was an app for finding dog parks, I don't remember. But they spent all their venture capital on fancy office furniture and espresso machines before they even launched the app. My brother works in tech and he says that happens all the time. People just burn through millions of dollars on cold brew on tap and ping pong tables. He works from home now, though, so he just sits on his couch with his laptop. His cat always walks across his keyboard during Zoom meetings. She's a calico, super fluffy, but she sheds everywhere. He has to buy those sticky lint rollers in bulk from Costco. 

I love Costco. Their pizza is so good, and you can't beat the hot dog combo. Have you ever tried their giant muffins? They're basically cake. 

But um, yeah. Sitting still isn't really the issue for me. I don't get restless or feel like I need to jump up or anything like that.

Or maybe it was an app for finding dog parks, I don't remember. But they spent all their venture capital on fancy office furniture and espresso machines before they even launched the app. My brother works in tech and he says that happens all the time. People just burn through millions of dollars on cold brew on tap and ping pong tables. He works from home now, though, so he just sits on his couch with his laptop. His cat always walks across his keyboard during Zoom meetings. She's a calico, super fluffy, but she sheds everywhere. He has to buy those sticky lint rollers in bulk from Costco. 

I love Costco. Their pizza is so good, and you can't beat the hot dog combo. Have you ever tried their giant muffins? They're basically cake. 

But um, yeah. Sitting still isn't really the issue for me. I don't get restless or feel like I need to jump up or anything like that.

inference.note: Ruled out F98.8. Patient demonstrates clear ADHD presentation: lifelong history of inattention (report cards from 4th grade), difficulty sustaining attention on tasks, loses focus during conversations and instructions despite making eye contact, mind 'drifts away' from tasks, excessive tangential speech with frequent topic changes, no evidence of hyperactivity/restlessness (rules out ADHD combined type), and functional impairment at work. The pervasive inattention across multiple domains (work, school history, conversations) with primarily inattentive presentation is consistent with F90.9 (ADHD, unspecified type). No evidence of specific developmental coordination disorder or other specified behavioral/emotional disorder that would support F98.8.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a long-standing pattern of difficulty sustaining attention and completing tasks, with onset in elementary school (confirmed by report cards from 4th grade). She demonstrates persistent inattention across multiple contexts (work logs, conversations, instructions from supervisors), characterized by mind-wandering, loss of focus, and failure to follow through on instructions despite adequate ability. She denies hyperactivity or restlessness. The chronic nature, early onset, functional impairment at work, and primary presentation of inattentive symptoms are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive type (F90.9).
